digest.component_or_area: store write seam / event append validation
propositions: The store accepts event bodies containing live credentials without validation, allowing secrets to be written to the append-only store and pushed to the shared tickets branch.

Because the store auto-pushes to a single shared ref, one secret-bearing event triggers GitHub push protection (GH013), which wedges the branch for all concurrent agents until manual intervention, presenting as transient contention rather than an explicit credential leak.

Multiple write paths bypass the append_event seam: the reconciler's inbound_translate writes Jira-sourced untrusted bodies by directly calling finalize_event halves, and txn/delete cores also bypass append_event, so a screen in append_event alone leaves external input unprotected.

The refusal mechanism must not echo secrets into error messages, logs, or on-disk artifacts, and must name the matched family and field location so operators can make informed override decisions using --allow-secret-pattern=<reason>.

Benign look-alike text (truncated placeholders like 'sk-ant-api03-...', regex literals, prose enumerating PEM banners) must continue to write successfully so the screen is safe to leave on by default without false-positive blocking of legitimate security incident reports.

The screen patterns must use fixed-width windows rather than greedy quantifiers to prevent entropy dilution by same-class padding appended after a real credential, and PEM patterns must be line-anchored to distinguish real pastes from prose mentioning banners.
